core.title: Declare what every URN-carrying test proves
core.given: A test file carries a URN identity header
core.when: The test is written, changed or reviewed
core.then: Declare beside the URN, in the profile's binding syntax, the plan obligation the test actually proves: an acceptance binding, or a user/system flow binding only for an e2e (journey) test.
prefer: Derive the binding from the plan artifact the test proves: the declared acceptance whose behavior the test exercises and asserts, or the declared user/system flow the journey actually walks
Use that exact plan identity: the acceptance URN in the profile's acceptance binding syntax, or the user/system flow URN in the profile's user/system flow binding syntax
avoid: Picking any resolvable acceptance merely to satisfy coverage
Changing the claimed binding to match a test that proves different behavior (rebinding for attribution); correcting a stale binding to the obligation the test truly proves is the fix, not this
Selecting or inventing a binding (new acceptance or user/system flow) merely to make an orphaned test bind or be attributable
unless: A user/system flow binding satisfies the rule for e2e (journey) tests, when the journey actually proves that user/system flow
core.why: A URN says which test this is; the binding says which obligation it discharges, and only that closes the loop the gate reads. The binding is a claim: truthful only if the test exercises the declared subject and asserts its outcome. A convenient but unrelated resolvable acceptance creates false coverage while still passing the structural check. User/system flow bindings exist because journeys prove a user/system flow; forcing an acceptance would push authors to invent check-only acceptances that pollute the plan graph.
evidence: Every URN-carrying test file has an acceptance binding or a user/system flow binding beside the URN (the stack's structural binding check reports no finding)
Any test bound only by a user/system flow binding is an e2e (journey) test
The test stimulus exercises the bound subject
The test's behavioral witness proves the bound obligation rather than an adjacent implementation detail
verification: Structural presence check (per file): a test file carrying a URN identity header must carry an acceptance binding or a user/system flow binding beside the URN header. Accepted forms: the acceptance binding (names the obligation the test discharges) and the user/system flow binding (alternative for an e2e/journey test, which proves a user/system flow rather than a single acceptance).
Files with no URN header are skipped; that finding belongs to test-carries-urn-identity.
Whether the named acceptance EXISTS in the plan graph is a plan-graph question a per-file check cannot answer; out of scope here (see acceptance-resolves-to-declared).

Truthfulness (stimulus exercises the bound subject, witness proves the bound obligation) is not structurally detectable: a convenient existing acceptance bound to an unrelated case satisfies the structural check while creating false coverage. Requires reviewer/LLM judgment.

Binding-kind check: a structural check that accepts any user/system flow binding does not establish that the file is an e2e (journey) test, the only case where a user/system flow binding alone satisfies the rule; that must be established by a test-tier classifier or reviewer judgment.
A stack's structural check may cover only part of the stack's test files; this limits automated coverage, not the rule's applicability to every URN-carrying test.
Disposition: strict. The enforcing gate fails on every finding of this rule; there is no advisory mode and no ratchet baseline.

values: URN identity header present but neither an acceptance binding nor a user/system flow binding
URN identity header present with only a user/system flow binding on a test that is not an e2e (journey) test
acceptance or user/system flow binding present but the test may not exercise/assert the bound subject

fires: Presence: a test file carries a URN identity header but has neither an acceptance binding nor a user/system flow binding
Binding kind: a URN-carrying test that is not an e2e (journey) test is bound only by a user/system flow binding (fires regardless of whether the test exercises or asserts that user/system flow)
Truthfulness: a URN-carrying test declares an acceptance or user/system flow binding whose subject the test does not exercise or whose outcome it does not assert
Truthfulness: a binding was selected, changed or invented only so the test becomes attributable
doesNotFire: A test file with no URN identity header (owned by test-carries-urn-identity)
Presence and binding-kind paths: an e2e (journey) test with a user/system flow binding (truthfulness review still applies)
Checking whether the named acceptance exists in the plan graph (owned by acceptance-resolves-to-declared)

The stack's local name for the e2e test role, the only tests for which a user/system flow binding alone satisfies the rule.

neutralityNotes: The convention is stack-neutral in substance; only the detector (bun_tester_discipline_detector), its JS/TS coverage and the concrete `//` header syntax are Bun-specific. The syntax of the test's own URN identity header is owned by test-carries-urn-identity and bun.json gives no concrete value for it, so no profile key is required for it here. How a test is classified as e2e (journey) is not stated concretely in bun.json; the core keeps that as a needs_new_observer fact and only requires the profile's local role name.
